label: Second copy step (orig[0] fed back), boosted when t/g/e/y are among the next few tokens to recall
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase. 92% of activation mass sits at recall_idx==1, the step right after <DEL> where the first original token is fed back in. Most of the rest is at recall_idx==2 (7%). It never fires during the original phase or on the delimiter step. Whether it fires, and how strongly, depends on which tokens are still to be recalled: t matters most (next_out==t has 9.3x lift, prev2_tok==t 3.4x), then g, e and y, and to a lesser degree j, w and c. The top activations (~5.5-5.9) are sequences like w j t t t <DEL>, where t fills the upcoming positions. The input token itself and first_tok barely matter. recall_idx==1 alone has recall 0.87 but precision only 0.17. Requiring t/g/e/y in orig(1..3) raises dev F1 to 0.47 (mass recall 0.77). The token dependence looks graded and spread over many tokens, so no simple boolean predicate captures it well.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig4=t (+5.02), orig3=t (+4.97), orig5=t (+4.16), orig4=g (+3.54), orig2=t (+3.35), orig3=g (+3.32). Lower it: in_first=1 (-5.93), to_go=0 (-4.55), in_tok=t (-3.41), next_out=- (-3.26).
